newsitem.title: ITALY: Top Italy anti-mob unit resigns over graft probe.
newsitem.headline: Top Italy anti-mob unit resigns over graft probe.

text.p: The head of Italy's anti-Mafia police unit has resigned after prosecutors disclosed that he was under investigation for alleged corruption, interior ministry officials said on Wednesday.
General Giovanni Verdicchio left his post on August 2, after hearings with prosecutors, an interior ministry statement said.

Verdicchio is under investigation in Perugia on suspicion of having received kickbacks from businessmen while he headed the main unit of Italy's fiscal police in Rome in the late 1980s and early 1990s, according to Felice Colombrino, a ministry spokesman.
Prosecutors in Perugia, in central Italy, listened to Verdicchio last week, and were planning to interrogate him in the next few days, Italian news reports said.
The interior ministry said it would soon name a new director for the anti-mafia unit, which runs investigations into the mob by all Italian police forces.
Verdicchio is a general in Italy's finance police.
